query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA, specifically yield strength and hardness, will change predictably with systematic variations in elemental percentages, achieved through a designed experiment methodology.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with a near-equal atomic percentage of each constituent element
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of elemental percentages using design of experiments (DOE) methodology
generation.conditions: Varied compositions of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr, with a range of +/- 10% variation from the baseline equal atomic percentage composition, tested under uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening due to changes in elemental percentages
generation.mechanism: The variation in elemental percentages alters the lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening effects, influencing the mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: A 15% increase in yield strength and a 20% increase in hardness compared to the baseline composition, when the percentage of Hf is increased by 10% and the percentage of Ti is decreased by 5%
generation.baseline: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with equal atomic percentages of each element, exhibiting a yield strength of 800 MPa and a hardness of 350 HV
generation.boundary: The range of +/- 10% variation in elemental percentages, beyond which the alloy's microstructure and mechanical properties may deviate significantly from the predicted behavior
generation.uncertainty: The actual mechanical properties may vary due to factors such as processing conditions, impurities, and experimental errors, which could affect the accuracy of the predictions

falsification_experiment.design: A designed experiment using the DOE methodology, with multiple compositions and replicates, to test the effects of varying elemental percentages on mechanical properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured yield strength and hardness values deviate by more than 10% from the predicted values for at least 80% of the tested compositions, the hypothesis is considered falsified
